💡 Ideathon 2026 Executive Summary: Reading the Road Disaster Relief & Critical Infrastructure
The Problem (Slide 2 & 3)
After floods or quakes, relief convoys (need 4.2m) get trapped on narrowed roads. Perspective distortion makes manual visual estimates unreliable.
The RoadSense Engine (Slide 4 & 5)
Ingests routine survey video, segments curbs, inverts perspective with IPM, and scales with anchors to output trusted metric width and confidence scores.
The Network Impact (Slide 8 & 13)
Auto-accepts 75%+ of roads so human effort scales effortlessly; identifies the single pinch-point fix that restores flow to hospitals.

Complete 15-Slide System Mapping

Slide 1 & 4: Core Innovation — RoadSense converts routine imagery into metric road width $W = ?\text{ m}$ with confidence scores.
Slide 2 & 3: The Threat — Perspective distortion shrinks roads; convoys need 4.2m; wrong estimates cause vehicle entrapment and isolate communities.
Slide 5: 5-Step Pipeline — Ingest → Segment → Rectify → Scale → Aggregate.
Slide 6: Validation Roadmap — Benchmarked against tape measures across urban, rural, and damaged roads; confidence predicts errors.
Slide 8: Cascading Failure — A single 2.8m mudslide cuts off hospital oxygen tankers; network optimization identifies the single fix.
Slide 9: Decision Support — Convoy clearance routing, what-if closure simulations, and targeted bulldozer hardening.
Slide 10: UN SDGs — Target 9.1 (Resilient Infrastructure) & Target 11.5 (Disaster Loss Reduction).
Slide 11 & 13: Triage at Scale — Auto-accept, Spot-check, Manual review; effort grows far slower than road length.
🔍 Human-in-the-Loop Segment Triage Inspector
